text: Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list … Only use this tool if you think it will be helpful … If the request is trivial and takes less than 3 steps, NOT use this tool.
note: ~3.9k chars of generic guidance; repeats the base prompt's write_todos section (A5).

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)
text: write_todos tracks your work; it does not deliver the answer. Whatever the user asked for … must appear as text content in a message after your final write_todos call.
note: Third description of "how a turn ends"; the scene agent ends with finalize_run.

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)
text: You should almost ALWAYS use this tool before using the read_file or edit_file tools.
note: Conflicts with "push context, don't fetch it" (frame header) and the skills list that already gives exact paths.

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)
text: By default, it reads up to 100 lines … Use pagination with offset and limit … First scan: limit=100 to see file structure … Only omit limit (read full file) when necessary for editing.
note: Third method for reading a skill (A2: follow continuation to the end; A5: pass limit=1000; here: scan 100 first).

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)
text: It is always better to speculatively read multiple files as a batch that are potentially useful.
note: Conflicts with the follow-up routine ("read only the skills, guides and files this request needs … nothing extra").

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)

src: tool descriptions: write_todos, ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep (deepagents library)
text: You must read the file before editing … preserve the exact indentation … ALWAYS prefer editing existing files over creating new ones. Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it.
